why: Puts back the Levels-grid push issue #324's step S5 removed from the session's construction block -- the sibling of `session-pushes-settings-display-to-the-hud`, and pinned for the same reason: a second writer of an application surface reads as ordinary wiring beside the gameplay pushes around it. This one is worse than a duplicate, because the two writers DISAGREE: a session's `deps.levels` is its OWN level system, which for a versus match is a single synthetic arena, so the last thing the HUD hears is a total of 1 -- read by `hud.ts` as "not a choice" -- and the empty host left behind after a versus match has no Levels button at all. Three independent nets catch it since step S8: hud-ownership.test.ts reports `setLevelSelect` as a session reaching an application route, loop.test.ts's versus-quit case reads every total the grid was ever told, and the call itself no longer exists on the `GameplayHud` the session holds -- so it fails to typecheck and throws under the harness's esbuild run, which is why its failing set is now most of the loop suite rather than one case. Re-anchored for issue #324's step S6. The old anchor carried the following line, the boot tail's `refreshStats(world)`, which that step renamed and pushed a comment in front of -- so the entry went FAILED-TO-APPLY. The anchor is now the `slot.setControllers` call delimited by its own newlines: indentation-scoped, which is what distinguishes this boot-time call from the identically-worded one inside `reassignSlot`, and carrying no neighbouring text for a later comment to break.
killedBy: HUD ownership boundary (issue #324) the gameplay session reaches ONLY gameplay members: the debt list is empty
quitting a versus match leaves a campaign-shaped Main Menu behind the empty host offers Continue/New Game/Levels/Versus, not the versus session's "Start Match"
